findings.title: Antigravity remaining_fraction out of range crashes the app in Int(Double)
findings.source: `agy /usage` JSON output (GeminiProvider.swift:71) and the generativelanguage.googleapis.com /models body (GeminiProvider.swift:94). decodeSnapshot tries both as AntigravityUsageResponse (GeminiProvider.swift:101)
findings.description: `remaining_fraction` is decoded as an unbounded Double. The clamp at line 151 only covers consumedFraction. The raw `rem` is multiplied by 100 and passed to Int(), which traps when the value is beyond Int range (for example 1e300 or -1e300). decodeSnapshot tries AntigravityUsageResponse first on every payload, so any response with `command.name == "usage"` reaches this line, whether it comes from agy or from the HTTP heartbeat.
findings.exploit_scenario: A hostile or compromised upstream returns {"command":{"name":"usage","data":{"groups":[{"name":"gemini","buckets":[{"window":"5h","remaining_fraction":1e300}]}]}}}. CachedFetch writes the payload to the DiskCache, and decoding it traps the process. Later launches that decode the cached payload inside the TTL crash again.
preconditions: attacker controls the agy output or the Gemini API response body
findings.impact: Local DoS: the menu-bar app crashes and can keep crashing on relaunch while the cached payload is still valid.
findings.fix: Clamp or reject non-finite and out-of-range values before converting: let r = rem.isFinite ? min(max(rem, 0), 1) : 1. Then use Int((r*100).rounded()), or validate remaining_fraction to 0...1 in the decoder.
findings.evidence: L150 `let rem = bucket.remainingFraction ?? 1.0`. L151 clamps only consumedFraction. L154 converts the unclamped `rem` with Int(). GeminiProvider.swift:101 always tries this decoder first.

findings.title: Unbounded Grok creditUsagePercent reaches Int() in the menu-bar label and crashes the app
findings.source: cli-chat-proxy.grok.com /v1/billing response, field config.creditUsagePercent (XAIProvider.swift:89-92, default preferGrokCLI=true)
findings.description: creditUsagePercent is decoded as an unbounded Double and copied unchanged into UsageWindow.utilizationPercent. Neither UsageWindow.init nor UsageSnapshot.maxUtilization nor AggregatesComputation clamps it. The UI then calls Int(percent.rounded()), which traps for values beyond Int range.
findings.exploit_scenario: The billing endpoint returns {"config":{"creditUsagePercent":1e300}}. The value becomes the weekly window and maxUtilization. The menu-bar label evaluates Int(1e300.rounded()) and the process traps. The cached payload keeps the crash going on relaunch.
preconditions: attacker controls the Grok CLI proxy response body
findings.impact: Local DoS of the whole menu-bar app, not only the xAI card.
findings.fix: Clamp or validate percentages at the wire boundary: guard isFinite, then clamp to 0...some max. Also make UsageWindow.init sanitize utilizationPercent so every vendor is covered.
findings.evidence: XAIWireTypes.swift:266 `let util = cfg.creditUsagePercent ?? 0.0`, passed as utilizationPercent: util at L270. UsageWindow.swift:20 stores it with no clamp. MenuBarLabelView.swift:41 `Int(percent.rounded())`.
